subject: Temporary egress window, retention SLAs, and subprocessor ledger
messages:
From: Sara Park <sara.park@acmehealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary egress window for failover testing + questions on subprocessors

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for walking us through the residency controls on Friday. As we proceed with procurement, Legal asked for a short write-up on how Redwood handles temporary cross-border processing during maintenance/failover windows. Specifically Acme needs:

- A maximum duration for any transient egress event (hours) and a guarantee it will be logged and auditable.
- Confirmation that subprocessors involved in the transient path are disclosed in advance and will be subject to the same DPA terms.
- Retention window implications for telemetry / audit logs generated during the transient window.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to a 72-hour maximum transient egress window for EU-anchored accounts and provide an ops runbook we can attach to the DPA addendum? Also, Legal would like a roster of subprocessors that might be activated during a cross-region failover.

Appreciate a short response and any artifacts we can share with procurement/legal.

Best,
Sara Park
Director, Platform Security
Acme Health

--
Attachment: sample_acme_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Park <sara.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary egress window for failover testing + questions on subprocessors

Hi Sara — great question. Thanks for the clear list. Below is a brief summary and I attached the ops runbook and our current subprocessor ledger.

Summary commitments (proposal):
- Transient egress window: Redwood can guarantee that any cross-region transient processing for EU-anchored customers will be limited to a 72-hour maximum for planned/maintenance-triggered events. Unplanned emergency failovers may require a slightly expanded window but will follow the same escalation/approval workflow and be documented.
- Auditing: All transient egress events are recorded in the audit trail with timestamps, routing decisions, and request provenance. We can provide a filtered audit export for the event window on request.
- Subprocessors: We will provide an activation roster (CSV) showing which subprocessors may be involved in routing or edge-caching during failover. Any subprocessor activated for an EU account will be contractually bound by our DPA terms or an equivalent addendum.
- Telemetry/log retention: Telemetry created during the transient window is retained per the account's logging policy. For EU-anchored accounts we propose a default 90-day retention for ephemeral routing traces, with the option to shorten on request for privacy/regulatory reasons.

Attachments: egress-runbook.pdf (ops runbook), subprocessor-roster.csv (current non-production roster)

Next steps: If this aligns with Acme's requirements, Legal can ask for a short DPA addendum referencing the runbook + roster and we can prepare a DocuSign packet. Kim (cc) will confirm the contractual language. Irene will follow up with operational specifics on the audit export format.

Cheers,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: egress-runbook.pdf, subprocessor-roster.csv

From: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Park <sara.park@acmehealth.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary egress window for failover testing + questions on subprocessors

Sara, Mateo — quick legal note on the proposed language.

We can accept a 72-hour maximum for planned transient egress events and will commit to providing the corresponding audit exports. A couple of clarifications we should capture in the addendum so both sides are aligned:

1) Emergency scenarios: define "emergency" and the approval path (we recommend Tier-1 on-call + customer security contact signoff).
2) Subprocessor equivalence: we will ensure subprocessors activated for transient routing are contractually required to comply with the DPA or an equivalent SCC-based addendum. If Acme requires prior notice before activation, we can offer a 48-hour notice for planned activations; immediate activations for emergency failovers will be documented post‑event.
3) KMS/keys: if Acme requires customer-controlled keys (BYOK/HSM) for cross-region payloads during the transient window, we need to scope that separately — current standard is Redwood-managed keys for hosted accounts.

If that sounds acceptable, we can produce a short DPA addendum template with three clauses: (a) transient egress window (b) subprocessor activation/notice (c) audit export format and retention. Please advise on the BYOK requirement.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal, Contracts
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: redwood_dpa_addendum_template.docx (doc stub)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Park <sara.park@acmehealth.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary egress window for failover testing + questions on subprocessors

Hi all — ops details from Engineering. A few items to make the runbook concrete:

- Audit export format: CSV export with columns [timestamp, request_id, model, route, src_region, dst_region, bytes, decision_reason]. We can provide sample export (1k rows) to validate.
- Activation roster: subprocessors that may appear in transient paths include our CDN partner (EdgeWave), a regional caching partner in APAC (CacheNexus), and cloud ingress gateways (cloud provider-managed). All names are listed in subprocessor-roster.csv.
- Telemetry retention: default 90 days for routing traces; longer retention lives in observability with RBAC. We can offer a temporary shortened retention (30 days) for Acme if required and can purge routing traces on request once the event window is closed.
- KMS note: transient route payloads remain encrypted in-flight. For any BYOK request there is an engineering onboarding that typically takes 4–6 weeks (key exchange, HSM integration, and test).

Operational ask for Acme: please confirm the security contact (name/email) who can approve emergency activations; otherwise we default to post-event notification with full audit.

Irene Choi
Principal SRE
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: kms-architecture.svg (image stub)

From: Sara Park <sara.park@acmehealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary egress window for failover testing + questions on subprocessors

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. Acme is comfortable with the 72-hour planned window and the 48-hour notice for planned activations. For emergencies we will accept post-event documentation but will need the on-call approval path captured in the addendum (we'll supply the approver names).

On BYOK: not required for initial go‑live but we will circle back once we scope PHI flows. For now, please proceed with the addendum including the runbook and roster attachments. Legal will route the DocuSign and I will attach your audit sample to our security packet.

Next action: Mateo, can you send the addendum + DocuSign packet and confirm expected turnaround?

Best,
Sara

--
Attachment: acme_requirements_v2.pdf (doc stub)
